note: Re-measured for Tnsor-Labs/brokoli#242 (lineage-profiling: batched latest-node-profile query, splitting the feature out of #239's N+1 GetLatestNodeProfile-per-node loop): net +2 from 327. Both are SQL-string-concatenation (G202) findings, one each in the new SQLiteStore.GetLatestNodeProfilesForPipelines (store/sqlite.go) and PostgresStore.GetLatestNodeProfilesForPipelines (store/postgres.go), the same 'latest per group' batched-query shape GetLatestRunsByPipelineIDs already uses a few hundred lines above each — and gosec already accepted that exact pattern's own G202 findings in this file (see the Tnsor-Labs/brokoli#8 entry below). Same reasoning applies here: the concatenated portion is strings.Join(placeholders, ",") building a parameterized IN (...) placeholder list (?/$N tokens only), never interpolated user input — pipelineIDs themselves are bound as query args, not concatenated into the SQL string. No new finding categories; no other file, rule, or line outside these two new functions moved. Re-measured for Tnsor-Labs/brokoli#38 (artifact reference types and the artifact store, milestones 1 and 2): net -1 from 328, so the ceiling is lowered rather than raised. The new pkg/artifact package adds no findings: its one file read is annotated #nosec G304 with the reason (the path is baseDir joined with two hex digests validated by parseURI, so no caller string reaches it), its directories are 0o750 and its temp files come from os.CreateTemp. The -1 is a G306 in engine/arrow_transfer.go that disappeared when WriteArrowJSON was refactored to stream through EncodeArrowJSON: the empty-dataset case used to be os.WriteFile(path, []byte("[]"), 0o644), and the function now opens the file once with os.Create for both cases. To be accurate about what that means: the finding is gone because gosec does not inspect os.Create's mode, not because the file became more restrictive — os.Create is 0666 before umask. It is a real reduction in findings, not a real improvement in permissions, and it is recorded that way so a later reader does not mistake it for hardening. Re-measured for Tnsor-Labs/brokoli#79 (keyset pagination for run history): net +2 from 326. Both are unhandled-error (G104) findings on two new s.db.Exec(...CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_runs_pipeline_id ON runs(pipeline_id, id DESC)...) calls added to SQLiteStore.migrate() and PostgresStore.migrate(), one per dialect. The index backs ListRunsByPipelineCursor's keyset walk: the pre-existing idx_runs_pipeline_status leads with status, so it cannot serve a query that filters on pipeline_id and ranges over id, and without the new index every page of run history would be a table scan. Same idempotent 'already exists is benign, safe to ignore' pattern as every other CREATE TABLE/CREATE INDEX statement in those two functions, and the same pattern accepted in every prior baseline bump below. Verified by running gosec on this branch (328) against the recorded 326: the only findings on the new lines are those two G104s, and no other file, rule or category moved. No new SQL-injection surface: ListRunsByPipelineCursor and ListRunsByPipelinePaged are fully parameterized (?/$N placeholders) including the cursor comparison and LIMIT/OFFSET, and the shared column lists they interpolate are package-level constants, never request input. Re-measured for Tnsor-Labs/brokoli#8: net +9 from the prior 302 (verified by diffing gosec JSON output between this branch and its exact merge base, matched on file+rule+code snippet rather than line number, since new lines earlier in store/sqlite.go and store/postgres.go shift every later finding's line number without changing the finding itself). That net +9 is 11 newly-introduced findings offset by 2 findings that only appear 'removed' because the exact query text they match on changed (see item 3 below) — not real fixes. All 11 newly-introduced findings are the same two already-accepted categories from #6/#7's notes above, not new categories of risk: (1) 8 unhandled-error (G104) findings on new s.db.Exec(...) DDL calls added to SQLiteStore.migrate()/PostgresStore.migrate() — 6 for ALTER TABLE runs ADD COLUMN pipeline_version / resumed_from_run_id plus the partial index on resumed_from_run_id (run-definition-snapshot and resume-lineage fields), and 2 for a new CREATE UNIQUE INDEX on pipeline_versions(pipeline_id, version) (closes a compute-then-insert race in SavePipelineVersion that this PR's resolveRunPipelineVersion makes far more likely to trigger — see that function's doc comment in both files). Same idempotent 'already exists is benign, safe to ignore' pattern as every other schema-setup statement in those functions. (2) 1 unhandled-error (G104) finding on api/handlers_pipeline.go's new h.store.SavePipelineVersion(p.ID, ..., "initial version") call in the pipeline Create handler — this is the exact same fire-and-forget style as the pre-existing, still-unguarded SavePipelineVersion call a few lines away in the Update handler; fixing only the new call site while leaving its sibling unguarded would be inconsistent, and error-handling that call site is out of scope for this PR. (3) 2 SQL-string-concatenation (G202) findings, one each in store/sqlite.go's and store/postgres.go's GetLatestRunsByPipelineIDs, are byte-for-byte pre-existing findings at the same locations (both queries already used strings.Join(placeholders, \",\") / a Postgres $N placeholder list for a parameterized IN-clause, not string-interpolated user input) that only re-triggered the snapshot-matching diff because pipeline_version/resumed_from_run_id were appended to both queries' column lists (fixing a real cross-backend inconsistency: Postgres's GetLatestRunsByPipelineIDs previously silently dropped those two new fields to their zero values while SQLite's had already been fixed); not a new SQL-injection surface. Two genuine gosec findings from this PR's own new code were fixed before this baseline update, not reflected in the ceiling: engine/artifact_store.go's LocalDiskArtifactStore initially had a G301 (world/group-readable artifact directory, 0o755 -> 0o750) and 2 G104 (unchecked os.Remove cleanup -> explicit `_ = os.Remove(...)`) findings in its first draft.
